items.title: BPD Criteria
items.content: **Borderline personality disorder is a pervasive pattern involving instability in relationships, self-image, affect, and impulsivity.** Mnemonics can cue criteria but do not replace a longitudinal, culturally informed assessment or differential diagnosis. Common criterion areas include abandonment sensitivity, unstable intense relationships, identity disturbance, impulsivity, suicidal or self-injurious behavior, affective instability, chronic emptiness, intense anger, and transient stress-related paranoia or dissociation. Dialectical behavior therapy has strong evidence for recurrent self-harm and emotion dysregulation and was originally developed for chronically suicidal people with BPD. Other structured treatments also have evidence; “gold standard” should not imply one universally superior treatment.

items.title: Ainsworth Strange Situation: Procedure & Interpretation
items.content: **Procedure first:** Ainsworth’s Strange Situation is a standardized series of infant–caregiver separations, reunions, and exposure to an unfamiliar adult. Trained coders consider exploration, distress, proximity seeking, contact maintenance, avoidance, resistance, and the organization of reunion behavior across the full procedure. The resulting secure, avoidant, resistant/ambivalent, or disorganized classification describes behavior in that relationship and assessment context; it is not a fixed child diagnosis, a caregiver personality label, proof of maltreatment, or a forecast of every later relationship. Distinguish this observational infant procedure from adult attachment self-reports and the Adult Attachment Interview. Culture, developmental status, stress, familiarity, and measurement conditions affect interpretation.

items.title: Effect-Size Benchmarks: Cohen Conventions
items.content: **Effect-size benchmarks are conventions, not universal labels of practical importance.** Cohen offered d values near 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8 and r values near .10, .30, and .50 as rough defaults when a field lacks better reference information. Interpret the estimate using the outcome scale, design, population, reliability, baseline risk, costs and harms, prior studies, and a smallest effect of interest. Report the effect definition, direction, uncertainty interval, and analysis choices. A "small" standardized effect can matter when outcomes are consequential or exposure is broad; a "large" effect can be imprecise, biased, or trivial for the decision. Benchmarks do not show causality, replication, clinical significance, or the probability that a hypothesis is true.

items.title: Anxiety, OCD & Trauma-Related Differentials: DSM-5-TR Cue
items.content: **Chapter placement is a retrieval cue, not a causal theory:** Anxiety disorders include conditions organized around excessive fear, anxiety, and related avoidance, such as GAD, panic disorder, agoraphobia, and specific or social phobia. OCD belongs with obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, which also include hoarding and body-focused or appearance-focused conditions. PTSD and acute stress disorder belong with trauma- and stressor-related disorders and require qualifying exposure. Separation into chapters does not mean the groups never overlap or share anxiety, learning, or repetitive behavior. Diagnose from the full syndrome, duration, impairment, exclusions, development, and context rather than the chapter label.

items.title: Schizophrenia Criteria: DSM-5-TR Cue
items.content: **DSM-5-TR retrieval cue: symptoms + function + course + exclusions, never one symptom or a dopamine story.** The active-phase cluster requires at least two of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior, and negative symptoms for a significant portion of one month, with at least one of the first three. Continuous disturbance lasts at least six months and includes the active phase; functioning is markedly below the prior level in major areas. Evaluate mood episodes, substances, medications, neurological or medical causes, developmental history, and cultural context. Hallucinations and unusual beliefs occur in multiple conditions, and schizophrenia is not dissociative identity disorder. Use the current DSM-5-TR for exact wording, coding, and exceptions.

items.title: Glial Cells
items.content: **Glia support, regulate, defend, and myelinate—do not reduce them to passive “glue.”** Astrocytes help regulate the extracellular environment, metabolism, synapses, and blood–brain-barrier functions. Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin and can support segments on multiple axons; Schwann cells myelinate PNS segments and support repair. Microglia are resident immune-surveillance and response cells. Ependymal cells line ventricles and participate in cerebrospinal-fluid physiology. Cell counts and roles vary by region; avoid the outdated “glia outnumber neurons 10:1 everywhere” shortcut.

items.expectedTitle: Type I vs. Type II Errors
items.title: Type I vs. Type II Errors
items.content: **Type I:** reject a true null. Chosen α controls the long-run Type I rate under the model and plan; p < .05 is not a 5% probability that the null is true. **Type II:** fail to reject a false null for a specified alternative; probability β. **Power = 1 − β** for a specified alternative, design, variability, and analysis. Fail to reject is not prove no effect. Multiplicity, optional stopping, assumption violations, and selective reporting can make nominal rates misleading. Balance errors by consequences; neither is always worse.

items.title: Test Security & Release
items.content: **Distinguish test data from test materials, then identify authority and risk.** Test data include scores, client responses, and examination notes. Under APA Standard 9.04, psychologists generally provide data pursuant to a client/patient release, with a narrow option to refrain for likely substantial harm or substantial misuse/misrepresentation; absent release, provide only as required by law or court order. Test materials include manuals, instruments, protocols, and questions/stimuli; Standard 9.11 calls for reasonable security efforts consistent with law and contract. Avoid blanket never-release rules.

The labels are descriptive organizers with limited demonstrated clinical utility. Diagnosis requires a pervasive, inflexible pattern, impairment or distress, developmental and cultural context, differential diagnosis, and evidence beyond a memorable adjective.

items.title: Evidence-Based Treatment Pairings
items.content: **Evidence-based practice is not a one-disorder/one-brand lookup table.** Integrate the best available research with clinical expertise and the person's characteristics, culture, preferences, goals, access needs, comorbidity, risk, setting, and prior response. Exam pairings can identify well-supported options: exposure-based methods for many anxiety presentations, ERP for OCD, behavioral activation or structured psychotherapies for depression, and trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD. Medication, combined care, family or systems work, and level of care may also be indicated. "Most effective," "gold standard," and "CBT works for everything" require a defined population, comparator, outcome, time point, harms, and evidence source. Shared decision-making, competence, monitoring, and revising a nonbeneficial plan remain essential.

items.title: Action Potential Steps
items.content: **Threshold → rising phase → falling phase → afterhyperpolarization → recovery.** At threshold, voltage-gated sodium conductance rises; sodium-channel inactivation and delayed potassium conductance then drive repolarization. Continued potassium conductance can briefly make the membrane more negative than rest. The absolute refractory period reflects unavailable sodium channels; during the relative refractory period another spike needs stronger input. Myelin permits saltatory propagation between excitable nodes. Exact voltages and timing vary—memorize the mechanism, not one universal number.

items.title: Intellectual Disability: Assessment Principles
items.content: **Intellectual disability requires converging evidence about intellectual functioning, adaptive behavior, and developmental onset; an IQ cutoff alone is insufficient.** Intellectual functioning concerns reasoning, learning, and problem solving assessed with appropriately normed measures and clinical judgment. Adaptive behavior concerns conceptual, social, and practical functioning in the person's actual cultural and community context. Limitations originate during the developmental period. Interpret any score with measurement error, language, communication access, health, education, opportunity, and test fairness in view. Severity and support decisions should not be inferred from a single total score. Strengths can coexist with limitations, and functioning can improve with individualized supports. The purpose of assessment is to answer a defined question and plan supports, not reduce a person to a number, predict a fixed life outcome, or presume competence or incapacity globally.

items.title: Cognitive Dissonance
items.content: **Cognitive dissonance is aversive inconsistency among relevant cognitions, commitments, or behavior.** People may reduce it by changing behavior or attitude, adding consonant reasons, trivializing, or reframing responsibility and importance. In Festinger and Carlsmith’s classic study, participants paid $1 later rated a dull task more favorably than those paid $20, consistent with insufficient external justification under those conditions. This is not proof that every mismatch must cause attitude change; choice, commitment, consequences, culture, and available justification matter.

items.title: Reinforcement Schedules: Application & Extinction Nuance
items.content: **Decode a schedule with two questions: WHAT advances it, and HOW predictable is the requirement?** **Ratio** schedules advance with responses; **interval** schedules make reinforcement available after time, usually for the first qualifying response after the interval. **Fixed** means a constant requirement and **variable** means requirements vary around a programmed value. Thus FR can produce a postreinforcement pause followed by responding, VR often supports relatively steady responding, FI can produce accelerating or "scalloped" responding, and VI often supports steadier moderate responding under classic laboratory arrangements. These are characteristic patterns, not rankings that every organism, task, or parameter must show. Reinforcer quality, deprivation or satiation, schedule value, instructions, response effort, prior learning, and concurrent alternatives change performance. A weekly paycheck is not automatically FI because salary usually is not delivered contingent on the first response after seven days; identify the actual response-reinforcer contingency. Intermittent reinforcement can produce more responding during extinction than continuous reinforcement in many preparations, but "VR is always most resistant" confuses different definitions and comparison arrangements. Resistance may be measured relative to baseline rate, time, responses, or omitted reinforcers, and those measures can disagree. FVFV is a classification cue, not a universal rate or persistence formula and not an intervention plan.

items.title: Record Retention & Legal Demands
items.content: **Record keeping supports continuity, accountability, billing, and legal/ethical compliance.** Include clinically necessary identifying information, consent and role clarification, assessment or treatment rationale, services and progress, risk decisions, consultations, billing, and disposition as applicable. ⏰ **Retention is jurisdiction- and setting-specific.** APA record-keeping guidance has offered general time frames, but statutes, regulations, payer rules, contracts, institutional policy, litigation holds, and rules for minors can require different periods. Verify current applicable requirements rather than memorizing one universal number. 🔒 Protect confidentiality, access, integrity, secure disposal, and continuity if the psychologist becomes unavailable. A subpoena requires timely lawful response and privilege analysis; it does not always authorize immediate disclosure.

items.title: Short-Term vs Working Memory
items.content: **Short-term memory emphasizes brief retention; working memory emphasizes temporary maintenance plus controlled use.** In Baddeley’s model, the phonological loop supports speech-based information, the visuospatial sketchpad supports visual/spatial information, the central executive coordinates attention, and the limited-capacity episodic buffer integrates information across systems and long-term memory. “7 ± 2” came from particular span tasks and is not a universal working-memory capacity. Different models define working memory differently; name the model and task instead of treating one architecture as settled fact.

Deficits in adaptive functioning that limit independence and social responsibility across conceptual, social, or practical domains. 3. Onset during the developmental period. Severity is based primarily on adaptive functioning and support needs, not a fixed IQ band or assumed school grade. Test scores include measurement error and must be interpreted with language, culture, education, sensory/motor status, and opportunity. Avoid outdated labels and deterministic claims about work or independent living.

items.title: Clinical Documentation: SOAPIER, Access & Retention
items.content: **SOAPIER can organize a note; it is not an APA-mandated universal format.** **S**ubjective report, **O**bjective observations or data, **A**ssessment, **P**lan, **I**ntervention, **E**valuation, and **R**evision can help a clinician connect services to clinical reasoning, but required content depends on setting, service, law, payer, employer, and professional standards. Document enough to support continuity, consent, assessment, interventions, response, risk and safety actions, consultation or coordination, and changes in plan as applicable, while protecting privacy and avoiding unsupported labels. The often-memorized "7 years after last service, or 3 years after a minor reaches majority" came from APA's 2007 Record Keeping Guidelines, was expressly subordinate to superseding requirements, and was archived by APA in 2019; it is not a current universal retention law. Check current jurisdiction, board, contract, payer, institutional policy, litigation hold, and federal requirements. Likewise, "the provider owns the record but the client may access it" is too broad. Under HIPAA, individuals generally may access protected health information in a covered entity's designated record set, including ordinary SOAP or clinical notes, subject to defined limits; separately maintained psychotherapy notes are treated differently. Access, amendment, custody, and ownership rules can differ, so verify the governing authority rather than using the mnemonic as legal advice.

items.title: Reliability vs. Validity
items.content: **Reliability/precision asks how consistent or precise scores are; validity asks whether evidence and theory support an intended score interpretation and use.** Internal consistency, interrater agreement, stability, and conditional precision answer different questions. Validity belongs to a proposed use in a population and context—not “the test” in the abstract. Imprecision limits defensible interpretation, but the dartboard slogan “validity is accuracy” is incomplete: modern validity requires a broader evidence argument and plausible alternatives.

items.title: Effect-Size Interpretation in Context
items.content: **Estimate -> Uncertainty -> Context -> Consequence.** Cohen's familiar conventions—d around .20/.50/.80 and r around .10/.30/.50—are historical rough reference points, not universal qualitative labels or conclusions about practical importance. A standardized mean difference depends on the comparison and standardizer; r gives direction and strength of a linear association but does not establish causation; and eta-squared, partial eta-squared, and generalized eta-squared answer different variance questions and should not be mixed. Squaring r is the proportion of variance accounted for only in the relevant simple linear setting, not a universal measure of importance. Interpret an effect against the raw outcome scale, measurement reliability, baseline risk, costs and benefits, duration, comparator, prior evidence in the field, study design, and the smallest effect that would matter. A small effect can be consequential when repeated or applied across a population, and a large standardized effect can be trivial, biased, or imprecise. Report the estimate with a confidence interval or other uncertainty information, specify the effect-size definition, and compare with domain-relevant effects. Statistical significance, effect magnitude, precision, and practical or clinical importance are separate judgments.

items.title: Reinforcement Schedules: Four Basic Patterns
items.content: **Four intermittent schedules: fixed/variable x ratio/interval.** **FR:** reinforce after a set response count; often high responding with a post-reinforcement pause. **VR:** reinforce after varying response counts around a programmed distribution; often high, steady responding. **FI:** reinforce the first qualifying response after a set time; classic laboratory performance can show a post-reinforcement pause and accelerating "scallop." **VI:** reinforce the first qualifying response after varying time intervals; often steadier, moderate responding. These are typical patterns, not guarantees: magnitude, deprivation, alternatives, instructions, history, and schedule details matter. Interval schedules still require a response after the interval.

items.title: Major Depressive Episode: DSM-5-TR Criteria Cue
items.content: **SIGECAPS is only a symptom-retrieval cue; diagnosis requires threshold, change, impairment, exclusions, and context.** A major depressive episode involves at least five symptoms during the same two-week period, representing a change from prior functioning, with depressed mood or diminished interest or pleasure among them. Symptoms include sleep, appetite or weight, psychomotor, energy, guilt or worthlessness, concentration or decision-making, and death or suicidal-thinking changes, but exact frequency and developmental wording matter. Establish clinically significant distress or impairment and assess bipolar history, substances, medications, medical conditions, psychosis, grief, culture, and safety. Bereavement does not automatically exclude an episode, and sadness alone does not establish one. Use current DSM-5-TR criteria rather than the mnemonic for diagnosis.

items.content: **CBT uses a collaborative, testable formulation linking situations, interpretations, emotion/physiology, and behavior.** Methods can include behavioral activation, exposure or experiments, skills practice, monitoring, problem solving, and examining the usefulness and evidence for appraisals. The aim is not forced positive thinking; it is more accurate, flexible responding and goal-linked behavior change. Protocols differ by problem and population, and technique should follow assessment, risk, culture, accessibility, preferences, and evidence.

items.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder
items.content: **Autism spectrum disorder — two core DSM-5-TR domains:** 1. Persistent differences or deficits in social communication and social interaction across contexts. 2. Restricted or repetitive behavior, interests, or activities, including sensory features (at least two types). Features begin in the early developmental period, cause clinically significant impairment, and are not better explained by intellectual disability alone. Specify language, intellectual, medical/genetic, catatonia, and support-level features as appropriate. Population surveillance estimates change by year, methods, location, age, sex, race/ethnicity, and access to identification. Avoid memorizing one prevalence figure as timeless or treating support levels as fixed descriptions of a person's worth or potential.

items.title: Erikson's 8 Stages
items.content: **Erikson’s historical sequence:** trust–mistrust; autonomy–shame/doubt; initiative–guilt; industry–inferiority; identity–role confusion; intimacy–isolation; generativity–stagnation; integrity–despair. The order is useful, but age bands are approximate teaching conventions—not diagnostic deadlines. Erikson proposed that each period makes a tension salient; themes can recur and later development can revise their resolution. Use the model to organize questions, not infer pathology from age or assume one culturally universal life course.

items.title: Negative Reinforcement vs. Punishment
items.content: **Classify a consequence with two questions:** Was a stimulus added (+) or removed (−)? Did the future probability of behavior increase (reinforcement) or decrease (punishment)? Positive reinforcement adds and increases; negative reinforcement removes/avoids and increases; positive punishment adds and decreases; negative punishment removes and decreases. Positive/negative do not mean good/bad, and the label depends on observed behavior change—not intention. Escape and avoidance are common negative-reinforcement arrangements; response cost is one form of negative punishment.

items.title: ADHD Presentations: DSM-5-TR Cue
items.content: **ADHD presentations:** predominantly inattentive, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive, or combined. Diagnosis requires a persistent developmentally inappropriate symptom pattern, several symptoms before age 12, presence in two or more settings, impairment, and consideration of alternative explanations. Thresholds differ for older adolescents/adults. Treatment is individualized and can include behavioral parent/classroom interventions, organizational and skills supports, environmental accommodations, stimulant or nonstimulant medication, and coordinated care. Medication does not “paradoxically calm every hyperactive child,” and no single combination is automatically best for every person.

items.title: Infant Attachment: Strange Situation Classifications
items.content: **Strange Situation reunion classifications describe an infant-caregiver relationship under a standardized procedure, not a fixed child personality.** **Secure:** seeks/accepts contact or comfort and returns to exploration. **Avoidant:** minimizes overt proximity/contact at reunion. **Resistant:** seeks contact yet resists or remains difficult to soothe. **Disorganized:** contradictory, apprehensive, freezing, disoriented, or otherwise lacking a coherent strategy. Code the full procedure with trained methods. A pattern does not by itself prove caregiver rejection, maltreatment, future disorder, or behavior in every relationship; culture, stress, context, and measurement conditions matter.

items.title: Sensitivity, Specificity, PPV, NPV
items.content: **Read the 2×2 table:** Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN), among people with the condition who tests positive. Specificity = TN/(TN+FP), among people without it who tests negative. PPV = TP/(TP+FP), among positive results who has the condition. NPV = TN/(TN+FN), among negative results who does not. Sensitivity and specificity can vary with threshold, spectrum, setting, and verification. Predictive values depend strongly on prevalence: the same test can have much lower PPV in a low-prevalence population.

items.title: Motivational Interviewing
items.content: **MI spirit: partnership, acceptance, compassion, and evocation. Processes: engaging → focusing → evoking → planning.** OARS—open questions, affirmations, reflections, summaries—supports conversation, but MI is not a bag of techniques. The practitioner listens for and strengthens the person’s own language for change while respecting autonomy; sustain talk is explored rather than argued away. Planning follows sufficient readiness and shared focus. MI is collaborative and directional, not persuasion by stealth or a guarantee of change.

items.title: APA Ethical Standards vs Principles
items.content: **APA Code:** General Principles A–E are aspirational ideals; Ethical Standards contain potentially enforceable rules. A: Beneficence and Nonmaleficence; B: Fidelity and Responsibility; C: Integrity; D: Justice; E: Respect for People’s Rights and Dignity. Principles still guide reasoning when rules leave judgment. APA ethics findings, licensing-board actions, civil liability, employment discipline, and criminal law are different processes; an alleged Standard violation does not automatically mean loss of license. Identify the authority, current provision, jurisdiction, and facts.

items.title: Substance Use Disorder: DSM-5-TR Criteria Cue
items.content: **Substance-specific application:** DSM-5-TR uses one SUD continuum rather than separate abuse and dependence diagnoses, but applies it to a specified substance class and 12-month pattern. The four recognition domains are impaired control, social impairment, risky use, and pharmacologic adaptation; current severity follows the number of criteria met. Craving was added and the former recurrent legal-problems item was removed. Do not equate physiologic dependence, prescribed exposure, intoxication, withdrawal, or any use with SUD. Tolerance and withdrawal rules vary by substance, some criteria may not apply, remission and controlled-environment specifiers have exact definitions, and co-occurring pain, psychiatric symptoms, safety, and social context require direct assessment.

items.title: TBI & Neurological Conditions
items.content: **Use three separate maps: INJURY, SEIZURE CLASS, and COGNITIVE SYNDROME.** **TBI:** A concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury, and loss of consciousness is not required. Acute severity classifications may combine Glasgow Coma Scale scores with loss or alteration of consciousness, post-traumatic amnesia, imaging, timing, and clinical context; a mnemonic or one score is not a diagnosis or prognosis. Symptoms can emerge later, and red flags require prompt medical evaluation. **Seizures:** The 2025 ILAE classification uses four main classes—focal, generalized, unknown whether focal or generalized, and unclassified—then adds classifiers and descriptors supported by the observed chronology and available evidence. Consciousness replaces awareness as a classifier, and observable versus nonobservable manifestations replace the older motor versus nonmotor split. “Grand mal,” “petit mal,” and “simple/complex partial” are legacy terms, and one seizure is not automatically epilepsy. Treatment depends on seizure type, cause, comorbidity, and the person; do not attach one medication to a category by rote. **Dementia:** Alzheimer disease, vascular contributions, Lewy body disease, frontotemporal disorders, and mixed pathologies can produce overlapping and variable presentations. A pattern may guide a differential diagnosis, but no single symptom proves an etiology. Depression, delirium, medications, metabolic conditions, and other disorders can impair cognition, so avoid the imprecise label “pseudodementia” and assess potentially reversible contributors.

items.title: Standard Error of Measurement
items.content: **Classical-test-theory SEM** is a score-unit estimate of measurement error, often approximated as SD × √(1 − reliability) for the relevant distribution and reliability estimate. Higher reliability generally yields smaller SEM with other terms fixed. A score interval needs an appropriate multiplier and assumptions; “±1 SEM guarantees a 68% true-score range” is too strong. Precision can vary across scores, forms, groups, and purposes. Comparing scores requires the standard error of the difference and a decision rule—not simply a difference greater than one SEM.

items.title: Prenatal Critical Periods & Teratogen Timing
items.content: **Remember TIME x DOSE x AGENT x SUSCEPTIBILITY, not a ranked danger list.** The germinal or preimplantation period, embryonic organogenesis, and fetal growth and functional maturation are useful broad phases, but exact boundaries differ depending on whether age is counted from fertilization or the last menstrual period. Early exposure is sometimes taught with an "all-or-none" rule: extensive cell loss may cause pregnancy loss while surviving cells may compensate. Treat that as a rule of thumb, not a guarantee of miscarriage or no effect. During organogenesis, many structures have exposure-specific windows of vulnerability, so structural malformation risk is often emphasized. Fetal development remains vulnerable to growth and functional effects, especially in the nervous system; "less vulnerable" never means safe. Developmental risk depends on the agent, route, timing, dose and duration, maternal and fetal biology, coexposures, and health context. Alcohol exposure can cause fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, and CDC states there is no known safe amount or time for alcohol use during pregnancy; that public-health guidance does not mean every exposure produces the same outcome. Tobacco, infections, medications, substances, metals, and environmental exposures have different evidence and risk patterns, so "alcohol is number one" is not a scientific comparison. Do not stop a prescribed medication after seeing a mnemonic: weigh maternal and fetal risks with qualified prenatal and prescribing professionals using exposure-specific evidence.

items.title: Telehealth Ethics & Practice
items.content: **Telepsychology requires clinical, technical, legal, and emergency competence.** 💻 Assess suitability, accessibility, technology limits, and alternatives for the individual client. 🔒 Use a documented privacy/security risk process. HIPAA does not “certify” products; covered providers may need appropriate safeguards and business-associate agreements. 📍 Authority to practice depends on where participants are located and current jurisdictional rules. PSYPACT may help eligible psychologists but is not universal permission. 🆘 Confirm location as clinically appropriate, plan for emergencies and disconnection, and know relevant local resources. 📋 Consent should address remote-service risks, privacy, records, fees, third parties, backup communication, and limits of the technology. Platform choice alone does not make telepsychology ethical or legally compliant.

items.title: Attribution Theory
items.content: **Kelley cue: consensus, consistency, distinctiveness—evidence, not a deterministic table.** Consensus asks whether others respond similarly; consistency asks whether this person responds similarly across occasions; distinctiveness asks whether this person responds differently to other targets. Patterns support person, entity, circumstance, or mixed hypotheses, but missing cues limit inference. Correspondence bias concerns over-weighting dispositions in some contexts. Do not pair it with a universal actor–observer rule: a meta-analysis found essentially no overall asymmetry, with moderator and valence effects.

items.title: Vygotsky's ZPD
items.content: **ZPD: what a learner cannot yet do independently but can accomplish with appropriate guidance or collaboration.** Cue: can do independently; can do with well-matched assistance (ZPD); cannot yet do even with current assistance. Scaffolding is a later instructional metaphor for contingent support that changes as competence grows; it is related to, but not identical with, Vygotsky’s original construct. Effective support responds to the learner and fades or changes when no longer needed. Avoid “all learning happens only here.”

items.title: Duty to Protect: Current-Law Decision Framework
items.content: **Tarasoff is the historical California anchor; the controlling duty is current jurisdiction-specific law and policy.** California Civil Code section 43.92 addresses a patient-communicated serious threat of physical violence against a reasonably identifiable victim and describes reasonable efforts to communicate with the victim and law enforcement. Other jurisdictions may impose, permit, or not specify warning or protective action, define covered professionals and triggering information differently, and recognize case law as well as statutes. Do not require the words "credible" or "imminent" unless the governing authority does. Clinically assess the threat and context, consult promptly without unnecessary disclosure, follow emergency and organizational procedures, take legally authorized protective steps, and document facts, authority, consultation, reasoning, actions, and follow-up.

items.title: Tarasoff: California Case & Historical Rule
items.content: **TARASOFF is a California case anchor; current jurisdiction controls.** In the 1976 California decision, the court held that when a therapist determines, or under professional standards should determine, that a patient presents a serious danger of violence to another, the therapist must use reasonable care to protect the foreseeable victim. The court described warning the victim or likely intermediaries, notifying police, and other reasonably necessary steps as possibilities whose adequacy depends on the circumstances. It did not create one national formula requiring direct warning whenever a client mentions harm. "Tarasoff I equals warn; Tarasoff II equals protect" is useful history but not a current multistate decision rule. States differ in whether a duty is mandatory, permissive, or not specially codified; covered professionals, triggering language, identifiable-victim requirements, immunity, permitted actions, documentation, and confidentiality rules also differ and can change. Threats involving self-harm, abuse reporting, weapons, forensic roles, schools, or property may invoke different authorities. Ethical confidentiality standards permit disclosure when mandated or permitted by law for a valid purpose, limited to what is necessary; they do not independently settle local duty-to-protect law. When risk emerges, conduct and document a competent individualized assessment, take proportionate safety steps, consult current law and qualified supervisors or counsel when feasible, and disclose only as authorized or required. Do not delay urgent protection while searching for a mnemonic, and do not promise that any single action automatically discharges a legal duty.

items.title: Teratogens: Exposure Risk Factors
items.content: **Prenatal risk depends on exposure, dose, timing, route, susceptibility, co-exposures, and the outcome measured; do not memorize a mixed "FATAL CATS" list.** A teratogen is an exposure capable of disrupting prenatal development under particular conditions. Alcohol has no known safe amount or time during pregnancy and can affect development throughout pregnancy. Some medications, infections, nicotine products, illicit substances, toxic metals, radiation levels, fever, and poorly controlled health conditions can increase specific risks, but they are not interchangeable. Maternal age is a risk factor, not a teratogen; ordinary stress and medically indicated diagnostic imaging should not be equated with known high-risk exposures. Do not advise abruptly stopping prescribed medication: current individualized medical and prenatal guidance is required.
